draft.title: The contingency approach
card: The contingency approach says there is no single best way to manage. The right approach depends on the situation.
Managers look at the problem in front of them, such as how urgent it is, how skilled the staff are and how much change is happening. Then they choose a style to suit.
The same manager may command in one case and consult staff in another. This is a sign of good judgement, not of being inconsistent.
This approach lets managers use ideas from other approaches when they fit. It does not say that any one of them is always right.
draft.remember: Contingency means it depends: match the management style to the situation.

a.q: Which statement best describes the contingency approach?
opts: The best style depends on the situation being faced
One style should be used in every situation
Managers should avoid changing their style once chosen
The best style is the one that gives staff the most say
a.why: The contingency approach holds that the right style depends on the situation, so managers adapt. Using one style everywhere is the opposite, as it assumes a single best way exists.
a.clue: Think about the phrase it depends.

b.q: Priya manages a bakery in Newcastle. During a fire drill she gives clear orders, and next week she asks staff to help design a new roster. Why does this fit the contingency approach?
opts: She chose a different style to suit each situation
She is inconsistent and has no management approach
She used the same style because staff expect it
She copied the style of the most successful bakery
b.why: Priya adapted her style to the problem: quick orders for an urgent drill, consultation for a roster. Calling her inconsistent is tempting, but the card says changing style to fit the case is good judgement.
b.clue: Look at how the two situations differ.

a.best: The best style depends on the situation being faced

b.best: She chose a different style to suit each situation
